chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ya'qub ibn Yazeed, from Ziyad al-Qandi, who said:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), and in front of him was a bowl of water containing black plums in their season. He said: 'A fever arose in me, and the fresh plums extinguish the heat and calm the bile (yellow fever), and the dried one from it calms the blood and removes the rumbling illness.'
ai.seo_question: What are the medicinal benefits of fresh and dried plums according to Imam al-Hassan al-Awwan (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Imam’s practical application of humoral medicine (Tibb al-Nafs), reflecting the Greco-Arabic medical understanding prevalent in the Shia scholarly tradition. It highlights the distinct therapeutic properties of fresh versus dried plums, emphasizing their role in balancing bodily humors such as bile and blood. The narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the integration of natural remedies within Islamic spiritual and physical health practices.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ziyad who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st and in front of him<sup>asws</sup> was a bowl of water in which were black plums during its season. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There was a fever with me and the soft plums extinguish the heat, and settle the paleness, and the dried from it settles the blood and takes away the illness of the rumbling’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja‘far from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from Ziyad al-Qandiy who has said the following:

“I once went to see abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and before him (the Imam) there was a bowl with black plums in its time (season). He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because fever increased in my body and fresh plums lower down fever, calm down yellowness (stomach acid). Dry plums calm down blood (excitement) and remove reverberating illnesses/”
